title: Replacement System Installations: Billing a New Line Set as a Change Order
content:
# New refrigerant line sets billed as change orders — Replacement System Installations

## Policy

A new refrigerant line set that the package does not include is billed on a Replacement System Installations project as a numbered change order, at the line-set change-order charge.

Work beyond the package scope is billed only through a numbered change order: a new line set at the line-set change-order charge worked out under this rule, duct modification beyond the allowance at the package's per-foot duct modification price, and other scope at the price written on the change order.

The line-set change order is charged once, under the change-order number the homeowner approved, and a change order the homeowner declined or withdrew is never charged.

## Business effect

Billing the change order places one change-order charge on the project ledger, carrying the approved change-order number and dated the day it is posted. The amount the homeowner owes on the project rises by exactly that charge.

| Homeowner's decision on the change order | Charged |
|---|---|
| Approved | Once, under the approved number |
| Declined | Never |
| Withdrawn | Never |

## Tool: `bill_change_order_a6215d22`

**Capability.** Charges one homeowner-approved change order to a replacement-installation project: a single change-order charge for the amount given, posted on the project's ledger under the change-order number the homeowner approved, dated today. The charge raises the amount the homeowner owes on the project by exactly that amount, and from then on the project's money history shows it as a change-order charge carrying that number.

**How it is invoked.** This is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `bill_change_order_a6215d22` and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `install_id` | The reference number of the installation project being charged, as shown by the installation project lookup for this homeowner | Text identifier |
| `customer_id` | The reference number of the homeowner who signed the contract, as shown by the customer profile lookup | Text identifier |
| `change_order_no` | The number of the approved change order this charge bills, exactly as it appears on the homeowner's change-order approval | Integer, 1 or higher on a change-order charge |
| `amount` | The change-order charge | US dollars, a number with no currency sign, 2 decimal places, always positive — the final charge already rounded to the cent |

**Return.** A receipt with `install_entry_id` (the reference number of the new change-order charge entry), `install_id` (the project charged), `change_order_no` (the number billed), `amount` (the amount charged, 2 decimal places), `posted_date` (today's date, YYYY-MM-DD) and `project_balance` (the amount the homeowner owes on the project once the charge is included, or null when the project could not be read). A receipt carrying `install_entry_id` means the charge is on the project.

## Illustration of a call (hypothetical values)

For a hypothetical project HP-1001 of homeowner C-2002 with approved change order number 1, a call with `install_id` HP-1001, `customer_id` C-2002, `change_order_no` 1 and the worked-out charge as `amount` returns a receipt showing the new entry, number 1, today's date and the new balance owed.
